beats.lead: The marathon legend is not in the main source
beats.text: Herodotus never mentions a run from Marathon to Athens.
beats.note: He does not mention a dying messenger either.

beats.text: The generals sent a runner from Athens to Sparta, who arrived the day after he left.
beats.note: He reported that the god Pan had appeared to him.

beats.name: Philippides
beats.role: The messenger sent to Sparta before the Battle of Marathon, named in some sources as Pheidippides.

beats.context: The Spartathlon distance from Athens to Sparta, run every year since 1983.

beats.text: The first known Marathon to Athens account is by Plutarch, centuries after the battle.
beats.note: He names a herald called Thersippus or Eukles. Lucian later names the runner Philippides.

beats.line: The legend is younger than the history.
